reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a tutorial on creating a YouTube channel, with screens showing account creation and YouTube Studio. Its money-related discussion concerns ordinary monetization eligibility, while requests to subscribe or follow are audience-engagement prompts rather than conditions for receiving money, access, or a financial return.

citations.quote: I'm going to tell you how you can create your YouTube channel.
You can create it from your smartphone.
you can simply see here. You can see a create channel option here. You can click on this create channel.
To manage easily you can download the Yt Studio application from the Play Store.

opening.argument: The presentation links an easy starting action to an income-oriented outcome. It says viewers can create a channel for free, do so from a smartphone, and use a Google account, while the supplied description explicitly frames the video around creating a channel and making money. That combination makes the channel-creation workflow function as the entry point to a low-barrier earning proposition, even though no concrete earnings amount is stated. The description also directs viewers to an external Google account signup page and asks them to subscribe and follow an Instagram link, giving the audience several participation steps alongside the income framing.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the activity a tutorial does not remove the promise-action structure. The video does more than explain a neutral feature: its title and description pair channel creation with earning money, while the account signup link supplies a concrete next step. The fact that no deposit is requested does not establish that the income proposition is substantiated; it only shows that the proposed entry barrier is low.

citations.quote: Earn Money in 2020
Create Your Google Account : https://accounts.google.com/signup
It's free to create a YouTube channel.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material does not show that money is promised in exchange for signup, clicking, subscribing, or following. The title and description merely state the subject as creating a channel and earning money, while the spoken material explains channel setup. The Google link is for creating an account, not a payment or claim flow, and no amount, guaranteed return, or financial condition is shown.

citations.quote: I'm going to tell you how you can create your YouTube channel.
Create Your Google Account : https://accounts.google.com/signup

opening.argument: Several low-friction signals appear together: the speaker describes channel creation as free, says it can be done from a smartphone, and presents money-making as the reason to create the channel. The description adds a direct account-signup URL and social links, while the frames show a guided sequence through account and channel settings. That combination can make an income pathway appear simpler and more immediate than the evidence supports. Nothing supplied demonstrates actual earnings, a successful withdrawal, or the conditions governing monetization, so the financial framing rests on an unusually easy setup story rather than demonstrated results.

citations.quote: It's free to create a YouTube channel.
You can create it from your smartphone.
Earn Money in 2020

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account treats the screens as reassurance, but the screens also underscore how little is required to begin: an account, a channel option, and settings. The video supplies an external signup route and uses a money-making headline without showing earnings or a withdrawal. Ordinary interface screens therefore do not resolve whether the earning claim is realistic or adequately qualified.

citations.quote: It's free to create a YouTube channel.
Earn Money in 2020
Create Your Google Account : https://accounts.google.com/signup

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary setup signals, not evidence of a scam mechanism. The material expressly describes creating a channel and managing it through YouTube Studio; it does not show a payout, withdrawal, guaranteed result, or deceptive claim. The absence of earnings evidence may limit the financial claim, but it does not convert a technology demonstration into a scam.

citations.quote: I'm going to tell you how you can create your YouTube channel.
To manage easily you can download the Yt Studio application from the Play Store.

opening.argument: Although formatted as instruction, the material also operates as channel promotion. The description asks viewers to subscribe, follow an Instagram account, visit a linked YouTube channel, give a thumbs up, and share with friends. The video simultaneously presents the creator as someone who can explain how to make money through a channel, and one frame visibly presents a subscription and notification prompt. Those calls to action turn the tutorial into audience acquisition: viewers are encouraged to participate in the creator's ecosystem while being shown an attractive, low-barrier income theme. The educational framing does not eliminate that promotional function.

GIVE A THUMBS UP :thumbs up: & SHARE WITH YOUR FRIENDS.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense characterizes subscription and follow requests as incidental, but the supplied description repeats them and adds sharing, a linked Instagram account, and a linked YouTube channel. A tutorial can still be promotional when its practical instructions are used to build the presenter’s audience. The visible subscription prompt supports that the engagement request is part of the presentation, not merely an abstract lesson.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a channel is not evidence that viewers are being defrauded. The requests are for likes, shares, subscriptions, and follows, not money, deposits, purchases, or access fees. The video’s substantive spoken content remains a channel-creation demonstration, and the subscription graphic does not show any financial return or false outcome.
